title: fix(runtime): GET /api/v1/packages honours the declared `enabled` query parameter
body:
Fixes #19394

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

Ruling item 2 of #17667 — comment `5651023067`, director seat, decision batch #126 item 1, maintainer 「同意」 to `1(2)·2A·3A·4B`. Items 1, 3 and 4 landed in PR #19364; this is the sibling the ruling assigned to 「the cli seat's sibling PR」. ⛔ Not re-adjudicated here. #17667 stays open — see *Card relationships* below.

## ⚠️ Two places where this PR does not match the dispatch order, flagged rather than silently matched

**1. The changeset is `minor` with a BREAKING banner, not `patch`.** The order said "if required, `patch` — ⛔ never `major`", and derived from the repo's own gates the answer is neither. The diff narrows a published wire accept set: `?enabled=1` used to answer `200` with every installed package and now answers `400`, and `?enabled=true` used to answer every row and now answers a subset. `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` records the launch-window convention — "During the launch window we ship breaking changes as `minor`" — and the sibling round in this very file, PR #19326, spelled exactly this class as `minor` + `**BREAKING**` + `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` + an ADR-0087 marker. This PR copies that. ⛔ No `major` anywhere.

**2. The `Clause-②` line carries the `(narrowing)` arm the claim comment did not.** The claim declared `Clause-②: no`; the value is unchanged and still `no` (nothing here adds a schema key, a closed-set member, a published export or a registry row — `check-widening-tells` reads 0 tells). The arm is added because the diff IS breaking in the direction `check-adr-0087-registration` judges, and that gate's own self-test names 「the `narrowing` ARM with no banner, no `major` and no `!`」 as a breaking declaration. Declaring the direction is what makes the marker owed rather than optional.

## ⭐ Which declaration this was read from, quoted

`packages/spec/src/api/package-api.zod.ts`, `ListInstalledPackagesRequestSchema`:

```ts
  /** Filter by enabled state */
  enabled: z.boolean().optional()
    .describe('Filter by enabled state'),
```

and the same file's docblock on that schema, which names the gap this card closes:

> ⚠️ ONE key is not there yet, and it is recorded rather than glossed: **`enabled` is still declared here and still unread by that door.** The same ruling closes it (item 2 — one filter line, the shape `status` already has) in the runtime, which is a different file and a different PR

Four things are read off that one line, and every one of them is a decision this door would otherwise have had to invent:

- **name** — `enabled`, not `disabled` and not `status`.
- **type** — `z.boolean()`: two spellings on the wire and no third.
- **default when absent** — there is NONE. `.optional()` carries no `.default()`.
- **absent vs an explicit value** — they DIFFER, and in the direction that is easy to get backwards. Absent means NO filter: every row, enabled and disabled alike, which is what this door served before. `enabled=false` is a filter and selects the disabled rows only. That distinction is not inferred — the first-party SDK already spells it, `if (filters?.enabled !== undefined) params.set('enabled', String(filters.enabled))` in `packages/client/src/index.ts`, so `?enabled=false` arrives here from a shipped producer.

## What changed

`packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts`, the `parts.length === 0 && m === 'GET'` branch:

- the filter is read before the registry, so a request-shape refusal does not depend on server state (the ordering argument the `version` gate one branch over already records), and after the capability gate, so a 400-vs-403 difference tells an unauthorized caller nothing;
- `undefined` stays reachable and never collapses into `false`;
- the row side is the row's own `enabled`, ⛔ not `status`. They are independent keys on `InstalledPackageSchema` and a row carrying no `enabled` counts as enabled — that schema's declared `.default(true)`. Spelled as a two-way partition so `?enabled=true` and `?enabled=false` sum to the unfiltered list; `p.enabled === want` would drop a key-less row out of both halves, silently, on a 200.

### The grammar is asked, ⛔ never re-spelled

The coercion is `parseBooleanParam` (`packages/runtime/src/query-param.ts`), the repo's one parser for a query parameter a schema declares `z.boolean()`. `GET /api/v1/notifications` reads its `read` key with it, and that key is declared character for character the same — `read: z.boolean().optional()`. So `enabled` inherits the rule that module's header states: 「A wire contract that declares `z.boolean()` has exactly two spellings; a third is refused rather than guessed」. A local `=== 'true'` here would have been a second dialect for one declared type, which is the `?read=1` defect (#6928) that module exists to stop anyone writing again.

Multiplicity is answered first, with the sentence this door already uses for a repeated `?version=` (`repeatedQueryParamMessage`, #17672) rather than a second one for the identical condition. A one-element array is one occurrence encoded differently by an adapter and is unwrapped; an empty array is no occurrence — both per that rule's own header, which is why the raw value cannot simply be handed to `parseBooleanParam` (it refuses every array).

### ⛔ Why this is not literally 「one filter line, same shape as `status`」

The ruling's wording for this item is quoted verbatim above and its *shape* half is the one thing here that does not transfer, so it is flagged rather than matched. `status` is declared `z.enum([…])` and read as `if (query?.status)` plus a string comparison. Applied to a declared BOOLEAN that guard and that comparison are wrong twice: the string `'false'` is truthy so the guard admits it, and `p.enabled === 'false'` matches no row at all — so the caller who asked for the disabled half would be handed an empty list with a `200`, which is this card's own defect pointing the other way. The filter is one line; its READ cannot be a copy of `status`'s. Nothing in `packages/spec` moves for this and no spec change was needed.

## Verification

Readings taken in this worktree, against `origin/main` at `c5d3d1d8b6`.

- **Gate family, derived from the real changed paths** (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, re-derived after the final commit): **59 derived · 58 run green · 1 NOT MEASURED · 0 UNRUN · 0 red**, reconciled with `--ran` carrying each exit code captured before any pipe. The one NOT MEASURED is the gate's own `exit 3` PREREQUISITE NOT MET: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` wants a whole-repo build ("Run `pnpm build` first. ⛔ This is NOT a pass: nothing was measured."). It is not a finding.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck` — clean, `tsc --noEmit` plus `check:test-typecheck` OK (the new test file adds no ledger debt).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime test` — **271 files / 3761 passed / 1 skipped**, and `test:repo` **2 files / 69 passed**. The new file alone is 27 tests. Repo-wide `eslint . --no-inline-config` also ran in full at this head: **6946 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings** — a whole-population reading, not a narrowing.
- **Reverse verification (one-off, not left in the tree).** Both halves of the read were removed on disk with `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, which proved each write landed before anything ran (anchor 1 → 0; blob `6db66d8936e0` → `21e49bbcb79b` → `207c948d69ce`), restoring the pre-card door: the parameter parsed by nothing and filtered by nothing. Direction observed: **red**, **17 failed / 10 passed**. The 10 that stayed green are the three declaration pins, the three absent-case pins — correct, since an ignoring door still serves the absent case right — and four preservation pins. Restore verified by blob identity against `HEAD` and an empty `git diff HEAD`, by the harness, ⛔ not by an exit code.
- The subject resolves through a RELATIVE import inside its own package, so no `dist` rides between the mutation and the verdict and no rebuild is owed on either leg.

## Card relationships

- **`Fixes #19394`** — this card only.
- **#17667 is not closed here.** It stays open until this lands and until its own `nextCursor` residue rides the release retirement batch; the card says so in as many words.
- **#19328 is not addressed here.** Those four residual install-door classes live in the `POST` branch of the same file. The diff does not touch that branch and the new test file asserts nothing about them in either direction — pinning them as `201` would freeze known residuals as intended behaviour, and pinning them as refused would widen a graded scope.

## Acceptance notes

Out of scope, noted and deliberately not filed:

- **`ListInstalledPackagesRequestSchema`'s docblock is now stale in one paragraph** — the ⚠️ block quoted above says `enabled` is "still declared here and still unread by that door", which stops being true when this merges. It is prose in `packages/spec/**`, a lane this dispatch is fenced out of, and the successor is named rather than hypothetical: #17667 is still open and its closing PR belongs to the spec seat. Not filed as its own card, because a card whose whole content is "delete a paragraph the open parent card already owns" is board noise.
- **`parseBooleanParam` refuses a ONE-element array while the repo's multiplicity rule accepts it as one occurrence.** That is why this door composes the two rules instead of handing the raw value over. `GET /api/v1/notifications` calls the parser directly and therefore refuses `?read=['true']`. Not filed: it is a difference between two house rules, not a reproducible defect against a declared contract, and no measurement was taken against that door. Successor: whoever converts the dispatcher domains per the incremental ingress lane.
- **The `/packages` dispatcher domain still declares no closed query-parameter set**, so an unrecognised NAME is dropped rather than refused. That is route 3, which the ruling considered and refused; #19364 recorded the same note and it is unchanged by this PR. Successor: the same ingress lane.

Landing waits for the seat. Nothing here flips ready, enqueues, arms auto-merge, requests review, or writes an assignee.
